questions.stem: All statements given below are true regarding Antigenic alterations, except:

options.label: A
options.text: Drug-induced anaemias, leucopenias and thrombocytopenias often have an autoimmune basis.

options.label: B
options.text: Viral infections, such as infectious mononucleosis, often precede autoimmune disease.

options.label: C
options.text: Neoantigens can arise from Physical agents such as photosensitivity and cold allergy.

options.label: D
options.text: Neoantigens cannot arise by mutation.

questions.solutionHtml:
Neoantigens cannot arise by mutation.
  • This is incorrect, as explained below.

Antigenic alterations:

  • Cells or tissues may undergo antigenic alterations due to physical, chemical and biological influences. Such altered or 'neoantigens' may elicit an immune response.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 210, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 166

questions.stem: You see a case of orchitis following mumps in the OPD. The pathogenesis of sperm antigens to damage the seminiferous tubules is explained by:

options.label: B
options.text: Sequestered antigens

options.label: C
options.text: Cross-reacting foreign antigens

options.label: D

questions.solutionHtml:
Sequestered antigens

questions.stem: You come across a patient with autoimmune hemolytic anaemia during your OPD posting. All of the given statements below are true with respect to Cold autoantibodies, except:

options.label: A
options.text: They are complete agglutinating antibodies belonging to the lgM class

options.label: B
options.text: They agglutinate erythrocytes at 37°C but not at four °C

options.label: C
options.text: Can be seen in trypanosomiasis and black water fever

options.label: D
options.text: Can be seen in primary atypical pneumonia

questions.answerText: They agglutinate erythrocytes at 37°C but not at four °C
questions.solutionHtml:
They agglutinate erythrocytes at 37°C but not at four °C
  • Option B. incorrect, as explained below
  • Autoimmune hemolytic anaemias: Autoantibodies against erythrocytes are demonstrable in this condition. Serologically, two groups of autoimmune anaemias can be distinguished, characterised by 'cold' and 'warm' antibodies, respectively.
  • The cold autoantibodies are, generally, complete agglutinating antibodies belonging to the IgM class (OPTION A) and agglutinate erythrocytes at four °C but not at three 7°C. (OPTION B) This condition, which used to accompany syphilitic infection frequently, is seldom seen nowadays. Cold agglutinins are also seen in primary atypical pneumonia (OPTION D), trypanosomiasis and black water fever. (OPTION C)
  • Warm autoantibodies are generally incomplete, non-agglutinating antibodies usually belonging to the IgG class and frequently seen in patients taking certain drugs such as sulphonamides, antibiotics and alpha methyl dopa.
  • In autoimmune anaemias, the red cells coated with antibodies are prematurely destroyed in the spleen and liver. Complement-dependent intravascular hemolysis appears to be a rare event.



Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 210, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 166

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents to your clinic with complaints of blurred and double vision, drooping of eyelids, facial muscular pain, and difficulty lifting her arms. She is diagnosed with Myasthenia Gravis. The statements below are all true, except:

options.label: A
options.text: Muscle fatigues are abnormal due to malfunction of the myoneural junction.

options.label: B
options.text: An antibody against the serotonin receptor on myoneural junctions of striated muscles is present in these patients.

options.label: C
options.text: The thymus shows lymphoid hyperplasia and numerous germinal centres

options.label: D
options.text: The pathogenic factor in neonatal myasthenia is the autoantibody passively acquired from the mother

questions.answerText: An antibody against the serotonin receptor on myoneural junctions of striated muscles is present in these patients.
questions.solutionHtml:
An antibody against the serotonin receptor on myoneural junctions of striated muscles is present in these patients.

questions.stem: You are posted in the Rheumatology clinic for a month and come across a Sjogren syndrome patient. The triad does not consist of the following:

options.label: A
options.text: Dry eyes

options.label: B
options.text: Dry mouth

options.label: C
options.text: Rheumatoid arthritis

options.label: D

questions.solutionHtml:
Gout
